subject: Geography
central_question: What makes development genuinely human, how can it be measured, and why do countries achieve different levels of human well-being?
in_scope_units: Difference between quantitative growth and qualitative, value-positive development.
Human development as enlargement of people's choices and freedoms, associated with Mahbub-ul-Haq and Amartya Sen.
Meaningful life and the centrality of health, education and access to resources.
The four pillars of human development: equity, sustainability, productivity and empowerment.
Income, welfare, basic-needs and capability approaches to human development.
Measurement through the Human Development Index and Human Poverty Index.
Gross National Happiness as an alternative qualitative measure.
International comparisons and categories of human development.
Role of social-sector expenditure, political stability, freedom and equitable distribution of resources.
banned_topics: Detailed world population distribution and demographic transition.
Detailed sectoral economic activities such as agriculture, manufacturing or trade.

known_pitfalls.correction: Positive growth is necessary but does not become development unless it improves quality.

known_pitfalls.claim: Human development is measured only by income.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter places people, choices, health, education and access to resources at the centre and presents several approaches and indices.

known_pitfalls.claim: A high HDI score proves that achievements are equally distributed.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter warns that HDI measures attainments but does not reveal their distribution.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 1(i) on the meaning of development.
NCERT Exercise 3(ii) on equity and sustainability.
NCERT Exercise 2(i) on the three basic areas of human development.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1–3 and a Project/Activity comparing corruption and human-development scores.
